newsitem.title: FRANCE: Two unions sign pact at BA's French units.
newsitem.headline: Two unions sign pact at BA's French units.

text.p: Two out of five unions representing cockpit crews at British Airways Plc's French airlines TAT and Air Liberte signed on Tuesday agreements to end a two-week strike and return to work on Wednesday, Air Liberte said.
The other unions said they were ready to continue the stoppage, which has grounded about half the flights of the two companies.
The company said in a statement that the strike would be lifted from 1000 GMT on Wednesday. A spokeswoman said traffic would only return to normal from Friday.
The three unions holding out were due to meet in a general meeting on Wednesday afternoon.

The agreement includes a 13th month of pay, a customary French condition of work, and two rest days per week, instead of the current one day. With post-flight rest time, the pilots and flight engineers will immediately get 8.75 rest days per month, rising to nine from October 31.
The flight crews were looking to get 10 rest days per month compared to between six and eight currently.

The unions have been striking to protest against BA's move to run the airlines as a single entity ahead of a proposed full-fledged merger. BA took over Air Liberte in January after the French carrier became insolvent.
